title: The classical Cantor–Schröder–Bernstein comparison incorrectly inserts computability.
details: Marks, version 2024-02-25, §5.2, p.30, paragraph immediately before the proof of Theorem 5.7, visually checked on 2026-11-08. The comparison says that injections between arbitrary sets X and Y imply a computable bijection. Ordinary Cantor–Schröder–Bernstein concludes a bijection, without an effective conclusion; arbitrary sets have not even been supplied computable presentations. Delete the word computable in this classical comparison. The actual Myhill theorem separately assumes computable injections respecting membership and its finite matching proof supplies a computable permutation. That effective theorem and its proof are not invalidated by the wording slip. The original assessment was made during planning. The Myhill entry adopts the effective finite-matching theorem under its actual computable-injection hypotheses and makes no effective conclusion for arbitrary set-theoretic injections.
